12. ANTEPARTUM HAEMORRHAGE

- 3.5%.

- 1/5 pre – Term deliveries due to APH.

Classification of APH:

Spotting:

Minor APH:

< 50ml.

Major APH:

50 – 1000ml.

Massive APH:

> 1000ml + shock.

Risk Factors of Abruption:

•2nd abruption 4.4%.
•After 2 events 19 – 25%.
•Pre-eclampsia.
•IUGR.
•Non – cephalic presentation.
•Multi parity.
•Low BMI.
•Assisted conception.
•I/U infection.
•PPROM/ PPROM.
•Trauma.
•Smoking.
•Drug abuse
-Cocaine.
-Amphetamine.
⇨Threated miscarriage 1 – 1.4% risk of APH/Abruption.
⇨1st bleeding is cause of APH
⇨Maternal Thrombophilia – weak association.
-Factor V Leiden.
-Prothrombin Gene mutation.

70% abruption in low risk.

⇨Unexplained APH has risk of:
-Pre Term delivery.
-IOL.
-Neonatal Admission.
-Hyperbilirubinemia.

Risk Factor of Previa:

Previous C/S.

Previous TOP.

Multi parity.

Multiple Pregnancy.

Smoking.

Uterine scar

Endometriosis

Manual removal. Deficient

Curettage. endometrium.

Sub mucous fibroids.

Assisted conception.

Complications of APH:

Maternal fetal

1. Anemia. 1. Hypoxia.

2. Infection. 2. IUGR.

3. Shock. 3. Pre – Term.

4. ATN. 4. IUD.

5. DIC.

6. Psychological.

7. B.T.

Assessment:

•Triage according to maternal condition.
-Cardiovascular.
-Bleeding.
-Associated pain.
-Fetal wellbeing.
⇨Detailed History and risk factors assessment if pts is stable.

Examination:

-P/A – Pain, contractions, presenting parts.
-P/S – Bleeding, OS, Cervical ectopy.
-P/V – when Previa is ruled out.

 

⇨Investigations:

Maternal:

-Blood tests + cross match 4 units of blood | in major/massive APH

CBC, LFT, U/E, coagulation screen.

-Minor – CBC & Blood group
- Kleihauer test is not used for diagnosis of abruption but in negative mothers for estimation of FMH

USG:

Placental localization.

Abruption.

Sensitivity – 24%.

Specificity – 96%.

PPV – 88%.

PPV – 58%.

Fetal:

-CTG – abnormal in 69% with abruption.
-USG.
⇨Admission.
-Spotting – Reassure.
-Heavier than spotting – Admit, work – up,

Discharge once bleeding settles.

⇨Steroid:

24 – 34+6weeks if Risk of pre-Term.

⇨Tocolysis:

Not recommended:

-Abruption.
-Major APH.
-Hemodynamic instability.
-Fetal compromise.
-Senior obstetrician should involve in decision making regarding tocolysis

C/I:

-Abruption is an absolute contraindication.
-Mild APH + Previa is a relative contraindication.
⇨ANC:

Switch to “High Risk” – obstetric led Care

serial growth Scan till its prove normal.

Birth:

⇨Expectant – CTG (N), Hemodynamically stable, Pre – Term.
⇨Expedite – abnormal CTG=> emergency C/S.

IUD – deliver immediately, C/S may be required.

⇨Unexplained APH with no Fetomaternal compromise => senior obstetrician should decide regarding MOD & TOD.

Fetal monitoring : by CEFM

Anesthesia:

⇨Regional – recommended until no C/I.
⇨General => if Fetomaternal condition is compromised.
-Stable mother but fetal compromise regional is preferred.
-Unstable mother GA is preferred to facilitate Resuscitation.

Active 3rd stage of labor is recommended.

Ergometrine if no HTN.

Anti D + FMH by Kleihauer is recommended.

Recurrent APH – repeat Anti D after 6 weeks.

Pts on warfarin/ heparin – No more doses.

-Further doses after consultation with medical staff & detailed assessment @ hospital.

Neonatal Management – Risk of fetal anemia – May need Transfusion.

Major/ Massive => senior pediatrician/ neonatologists.

Minor => pediatric support only.

Abruption/ Vasa previa => senior pediatrician / Neonatologist => may need tx.

Anterior placenta => experienced pediatrician / Neonatologist.

APH @ 24 – 26 weeks:

•Mother is priority.
•Senior pediatrician / Neonatologist should involve in counselling.
•Conservative treatment if mother is stable.

Post – Natal F/U:

•4 – 6 weeks.

Principles of Management of APH:

1. Call for help:(MDT)

-Experienced midwife.
-Obstetric middle grade, alert consultant.
-Anesthesia middle grade, alert consultant.
-Blood tx lab.
-Porters of specimen/ blood.
-Designate 1 person for documentation.

2. Initiate Management:

-A, B, C, D, E approach
-D = decide delivery after fetal assessment.

3. 4 Pillars of Management:

-Communication.
-Resuscitation.
-Evaluation + Monitoring.
-Arrest bleeding and delivery of fetus.

Fluid Replacement and Blood & blood products:

A – Airway + O2 10 – 15 liter/min.

B – Breathing.

C – Circulation 2 – 14G cannulas.

Left lateral.

Keep warm.

 

Fluids:

•Crystalloids = up to 2 lit
•Colloid = 1 – 2 lit.
•Blood – cross matched if not available – O-ve.
•FFP

- 4 units of FFP (12 – 15ml/kg or total 1 liter).

- For 6 units of red cells.

- If PT/ APTT > 1.5 of mean control.

•PLT concentrate =if < 50 x 109.
•Cryoprecipitate =if fibrinogen < 1g/lit.

Availability of Blood:

•O negative = immediately.
•Cross matched = 15 min.
•Properly screened = 1hr.

Therapeutic Goals:

•Hb > 8g/dl.
•PLT > 75 x 109.
•PT < 1.5.
•APTT < 1.5.
•Fibrinogen > 1.

Colloids:

•Haemaccel.
•Dextran.
•Albumin.
•Mannitol.
•6% HES.
